ui.summary: Renders sections as native details elements.

manifest.name: alert-dialog
manifest.title: AlertDialog
manifest.description: The AlertDialog renderer and its options.

ui.name: alert-dialog
ui.summary: Renders a modal requiring an explicit confirm or cancel.
ui.guidance: Both buttons submit the enclosing `form method="dialog"` with a value, so the platform closes the dialog and records the choice in `returnValue`. They were once type="button" with no handler, which left a keyboard or pointer user inside a modal with no way out; a destructive confirmation is the last place to depend on JavaScript having loaded. role="alertdialog" with a described message is what makes a screen reader announce the consequence rather than just the title. Cancel is first in the DOM, so the platform's own initial focus lands on the safe choice. A destructive dialog that opens with Delete focused turns a stray Enter - the key the user just pressed to open it - into the deletion.
ui.keyboard: Escape closes the native dialog, and Cancel is first in the DOM so the platform's initial focus - and a stray Enter - lands on the safe choice.

manifest.name: aspect-ratio
manifest.title: AspectRatio
manifest.description: The AspectRatio renderer and its options.

ui.name: aspect-ratio
ui.summary: Reserves the box a medium will occupy.
ui.guidance: This exists to stop layout shift: without a reserved box the page reflows the moment an image or embed arrives, moving whatever the user was about to click. RatioAuto is the honest name for declining to reserve, rather than a default that hides the cost.

manifest.name: attachment
manifest.title: Attachment
manifest.description: The Attachment renderer and its options.

ui.name: attachment
ui.summary: Renders one file row.
ui.guidance: The name is the link text, not "download": a screen reader's link list shows link text out of context, and forty links all reading "download" are indistinguishable.

manifest.name: back-link
manifest.title: BackLink
manifest.description: The BackLink renderer and its options.

ui.name: back-link
ui.summary: Renders a link up to the parent view.

manifest.name: badge

ui.name: badge
ui.summary: A small state pill: Kind picks the semantic colour.

manifest.name: banner
manifest.title: Banner

ui.name: banner
ui.summary: A full-bleed shell notice (impersonation, billing).

manifest.name: breadcrumbs
manifest.title: Breadcrumbs
manifest.description: The Breadcrumbs renderer and its options.

ui.name: breadcrumbs
ui.summary: Renders an ordered trail to the current page.
ui.guidance: It is an <ol> because the order is the meaning, and the separators are aria-hidden: a screen reader announces list position already, so reading a slash between every item is noise.

manifest.name: calendar
manifest.title: Calendar and date pickers
manifest.description: Native date, datetime-local and two-input range fields stay authoritative; Cally adds a calendar in a first-party popover. Also a static month grid, an agenda scheduler and a checkbox availability grid.

ui.name: availability-grid
ui.summary: Renders slots as real checkboxes.
ui.guidance: Checkboxes inside a fieldset, not clickable divs: the selection submits with no JavaScript, every slot is reachable by keyboard, and the legend associates the question with the answers. A grid of divs with click handlers has none of those properties and looks the same.

ui.name: date-picker
ui.summary: Renders a native date input plus an optional calendar.
ui.guidance: The input is the control. With no JavaScript the user types a date and the form submits; the platform supplies the format, the keyboard entry and the mobile date wheel. Cally adds a calendar in a first-party popover, and it writes into the same input rather than replacing it - which is why the value cannot diverge from what the server receives.
ui.keyboard: The native input keeps the platform's own keyboard entry, and Escape closes the calendar popover and returns focus to the trigger.

ui.name: date-range-picker
ui.summary: Renders two native date inputs plus a range calendar.
ui.guidance: Two inputs rather than one string: a range submitted as one value has to be parsed and re-validated, and a partially filled range cannot be represented at all. The server owns start<=end regardless of what the calendar allowed.
ui.keyboard: The native input keeps the platform's own keyboard entry, and Escape closes the calendar popover and returns focus to the trigger.

ui.name: date-time-picker
ui.summary: Renders a native datetime-local input plus a calendar.
ui.guidance: The calendar contributes only the date half. It writes nothing until a time exists too, because a datetime with a guessed midnight is a wrong answer that looks like a right one - and the user never chose it.
ui.keyboard: The native input keeps the platform's own keyboard entry, and Escape closes the calendar popover and returns focus to the trigger.

ui.name: month-grid
ui.summary: Renders a month as a table.
ui.guidance: A calendar is tabular data - days across, weeks down - so it is a <table> with real column headers. A grid of divs looks identical and tells a screen reader nothing about which weekday a date falls on, which is the one thing a calendar exists to convey.

ui.name: scheduler
ui.summary: Renders a day-grouped agenda.
ui.guidance: An agenda list, not a pixel grid: a time grid positions entries by offset, which conveys duration visually and nothing at all to a screen reader, and collapses badly on a phone. The list states each entry's times as text.

manifest.name: card
manifest.title: Card
manifest.description: The Card renderer and its options.

ui.name: card
ui.summary: The bordered container every panel sits in.

ui.name: card-footer
ui.summary: Renders a trailing action row.

ui.name: card-header
ui.summary: Renders a title row with optional trailing actions.

manifest.name: carousel
manifest.title: Carousel
manifest.description: CSS scroll snap over a plain list. Autoplay is off by default, pauses on hover and focus, and never runs under reduced motion. The dots are real anchors to each slide.

ui.name: carousel
ui.summary: Renders a horizontally scrollable region.
ui.guidance: It is CSS scroll snap over a plain list, so every slide is reachable by scrolling, by keyboard, and with no JavaScript at all. It is deliberately not an ARIA carousel widget: the browser's own scroll container already gives keyboard scrolling and a scrollbar, and re-implementing that as a slideshow would hide the slides that are currently off screen.
ui.keyboard: The scroller is focusable, so arrow keys scroll between slides; no slideshow key model is layered over the browser's own scrolling.

ui.name: carousel-dots
ui.summary: Renders links to each slide.
ui.guidance: They are real anchors to each slide's id, so they work with no JavaScript and the browser scrolls the slide into view itself. Each carries the position as text: a row of unlabelled dots is a set of controls a screen reader cannot tell apart.

ui.name: carousel-slide
ui.summary: Renders one slide.

manifest.name: center
manifest.title: Center
manifest.description: The Center renderer and its options.

ui.name: center
ui.summary: Centres its content horizontally within a constrained measure.
ui.guidance: It does not centre text. Centred body copy forces the eye to find a new left edge on every line, which is why this only centres the block.

manifest.name: char-counter
manifest.title: CharCounter
manifest.description: The CharCounter renderer and its options.

ui.name: char-counter
ui.summary: Renders a live character count for a length-limited control.
ui.guidance: The native maxlength on the control is what actually enforces the limit, and the server enforces it again. This is only the readout, so a user who has JavaScript disabled still cannot exceed the limit - they simply do not see the running total. aria-live is polite and the region announces only the count, so a screen reader is not interrupted on every keystroke.

manifest.name: chart
manifest.title: Charts
manifest.description: Bar, line, area, donut and sparkline figures. Each renders a caption, summary and semantic data table always; the Chart.js visual is added on top only when the engine loads.

ui.name: area-chart
ui.summary: Renders area data as a figure: caption, summary, semantic table, and a hidden visual mount.
ui.guidance: The order is the design. The table is the chart - it is rendered first, always present, and never hidden by default. The canvas is an enhancement that becomes visible only after the engine initialises successfully, and the adapter reads its data *out of that table* rather than from a duplicate payload, so the picture and the numbers cannot drift apart. If the engine never loads, the page is a table: complete, readable, and printable. BarChartOpts, LineChartOpts, AreaChartOpts, DonutChartOpts and SparklineOpts are separate types rather than one type with a shape field, so a caller cannot ask for a donut with two axes and the gallery cannot render a shape nobody declared.

ui.name: bar-chart
ui.summary: Renders bar data as a figure: caption, summary, semantic table, and a hidden visual mount.

ui.name: chart-legend
ui.summary: Names each series in text with its colour swatch.
ui.guidance: The swatch is decoration: colour alone cannot distinguish series for a colour-blind reader, so the label is what carries the identity.

manifest.name: chat-log
manifest.title: ChatLog
manifest.description: The ChatLog renderer and its options.

ui.name: chat-log
ui.summary: Renders the transcript as a polite live region.
ui.guidance: Polite, never assertive: an assertive log interrupts the screen reader on every token of a streaming response, which makes the page unusable. role=log is the specific one for an append-only transcript - it tells assistive technology that only additions matter, so earlier messages are not re-read.

manifest.name: chat-message
manifest.title: ChatMessage
manifest.description: The ChatMessage renderer and its options.

ui.name: chat-message
ui.summary: Renders one message.

manifest.name: checkbox
manifest.title: Checkbox
manifest.description: The Checkbox renderer and its options.

ui.name: checkbox
ui.summary: A labelled checkbox.

manifest.name: checkbox-group
manifest.title: CheckboxGroup
manifest.description: The CheckboxGroup renderer and its options.

ui.name: checkbox-group
ui.summary: Renders related checkboxes inside a fieldset.
ui.guidance: A fieldset with a legend is what associates the group's question with each answer. Wrapping them in a div with a heading looks identical and tells a screen-reader user nothing about what the checkboxes belong to.

manifest.name: collapsible
manifest.title: Collapsible
manifest.description: The Collapsible renderer and its options.

ui.name: collapsible
ui.summary: Renders a native details/summary around a region.
ui.guidance: It is the same platform primitive as Disclosure, differing only in that the summary is dressed as a button and the region carries a caller-supplied id. No JavaScript at all: the platform supplies the toggle, the button semantics, keyboard activation and the expanded-state announcement, which is why this component declares no engine and needs no native fallback.

manifest.name: color-input
manifest.title: ColorInput
manifest.description: The ColorInput renderer and its options.

ui.name: color-input
ui.summary: Renders a native colour input paired with its hex value.
ui.guidance: The hex text is shown because a swatch alone cannot be read, compared, copied, or communicated - and it is the value the user will paste elsewhere.

manifest.name: column-header
manifest.title: ColumnHeader
manifest.description: The ColumnHeader renderer and its options.

ui.name: column-header
ui.summary: Renders a th with sort semantics.
ui.guidance: aria-sort is what tells a screen-reader user which column orders the table and in which direction. Without it a sorted table is indistinguishable from an unsorted one, and the little arrow glyph is invisible to them.

manifest.name: combobox
manifest.title: Combobox
manifest.description: The Combobox renderer and its options.

ui.name: combobox
ui.summary: Renders a text input backed by a native datalist.
ui.guidance: datalist is the engine-free choice: the browser supplies the filtering, the popup, keyboard navigation and mobile behaviour, and the field still submits a value with JavaScript disabled. A hand-built listbox has to reimplement all of that and usually ships without the keyboard half.

manifest.name: command
manifest.title: Command palette
manifest.description: A search form in a native dialog where every command is a link. The combobox roles are applied by the controller that implements them, never rendered as an unfulfilled promise.

ui.name: command-group
ui.summary: Renders a titled group of commands.

ui.name: command-item
ui.summary: Renders one command as a link.
ui.guidance: A link, because every command has a destination. Rendering it as a div with a click handler would make it unreachable by keyboard, un-middle-clickable, and invisible to a screen reader's list of links.

ui.name: command-palette
ui.summary: Renders a searchable command dialog.
ui.guidance: The markup is a real form pointing at a real search page, inside a native dialog. With no JavaScript the palette is a search form that works; with it, the input becomes a combobox over a listbox and Cmd/Ctrl-K opens the dialog. The combobox roles are added by the controller, not baked into the markup, because an input claiming role="combobox" with no active descendant and no key handling is worse than a plain text field.
ui.keyboard: Cmd/Ctrl-K opens the palette, ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the active option, Home/End jump to the ends, and Enter follows the highlighted command or submits the search when nothing is highlighted.

manifest.name: comment
manifest.title: Comment
manifest.description: The Comment renderer and its options.

ui.name: comment
ui.summary: Renders one comment.

manifest.name: comment-thread
manifest.title: CommentThread
manifest.description: The CommentThread renderer and its options.

ui.name: comment-thread
ui.summary: Groups comments into a named region.
ui.guidance: It is not a live region: a thread rendered with the page has nothing new to announce. ChatLog is the live counterpart, for messages arriving after load.

manifest.name: composer
manifest.title: Composer
manifest.description: The Composer renderer and its options.

ui.name: composer
ui.summary: Renders a message form.
ui.guidance: It is a real form with a submit button, so a message can be sent with no JavaScript and with the keyboard alone. There is no Enter-to-send here: a textarea where Enter submits makes multi-line messages impossible to write, and a caller who wants it can add it deliberately.

manifest.name: confirm-action
manifest.title: ConfirmAction
manifest.description: The ConfirmAction renderer and its options.

ui.name: confirm-action
ui.summary: Renders a trigger plus the dialog that gates its request.
ui.guidance: This replaces hx-confirm, which calls window.confirm: an OS dialog that cannot be translated, cannot be styled, cannot be tested through the DOM, and on some platforms offers a "prevent further dialogs" checkbox that silently disables every subsequent confirmation on the page.
ui.keyboard: Escape closes the confirmation dialog, and initial focus lands on Cancel so a stray Enter cannot confirm.

manifest.name: container
manifest.title: Container
manifest.description: The Container renderer and its options.

ui.name: container
ui.summary: Renders a width-constrained wrapper.

manifest.name: context-menu
manifest.title: ContextMenu
manifest.description: The ContextMenu renderer and its options.

ui.name: context-menu
ui.summary: Renders a region whose commands are reachable by right-click and by an explicit trigger.
ui.guidance: The trigger is a real DropdownMenu, so the keyboard path is the same well-tested one every other menu uses; right-click is the addition, not the mechanism.
ui.keyboard: Right-click opens the menu, and its trigger carries the standard menu keys: Escape closes, ArrowUp/ArrowDown and Home/End move between commands, and a printable character jumps to the next matching one.

manifest.name: cursor-pagination
manifest.title: CursorPagination
manifest.description: The CursorPagination renderer and its options.

ui.name: cursor-pagination
ui.summary: Renders previous/next controls for a keyset-paged list.

manifest.name: data-grid
manifest.title: Data grid
manifest.description: A progressive layer over DataTable: roving cell focus, column visibility and width, and windowed row fetches. Sort, search and pagination stay server-owned, and the pager is never removed.

ui.name: column-picker
ui.summary: Renders per-column visibility checkboxes inside a native disclosure.
ui.guidance: Checkboxes in a details element, not a custom menu: the state is a set of independent toggles, which is exactly what a checkbox group is, and the platform already supplies the keyboard model. The picker starts hidden because hiding a column has no effect without the controller.

ui.name: data-grid
ui.summary: Renders the grid surface.
ui.guidance: The table is a real table with real headers, and the enhancement adds cell focus and column controls on top of it. It is deliberately not role="grid": that role promises a full two-dimensional keyboard model, and claiming it while the page still behaves like a table is worse for a screen-reader user than the honest table semantics they already understand.
ui.keyboard: Arrow keys move cell focus, Home/End jump to the row's ends (with Ctrl/Cmd, to the grid's first or last cell) and PageUp/PageDown move ten rows; a cell containing a text control keeps its own keys.

ui.name: grid-toolbar
ui.summary: Renders search plus the column picker trigger.

manifest.name: data-table
manifest.title: DataTable
manifest.description: The DataTable renderer and its options.

ui.name: data-table
ui.summary: Renders the full table surface.

manifest.name: date-field
manifest.title: DateField
manifest.description: The DateField renderer and its options.

ui.name: date-field
ui.summary: Renders a native date input.
ui.guidance: The platform picker already handles locale format, keyboard entry, and the mobile date wheel; a custom calendar has to re-earn all three and usually loses the keyboard.

manifest.name: date-range-field
manifest.title: DateRangeField
manifest.description: The DateRangeField renderer and its options.

ui.name: date-range-field
ui.summary: Renders a start and end date as two native date inputs.
ui.guidance: The end input's min is bound to the start value by the Alpine behaviour, but the server still validates the ordering: a range that only makes sense because the browser prevented the mistake is not validated at all.

manifest.name: date-time-field
manifest.title: DateTimeField
manifest.description: The DateTimeField renderer and its options.

ui.name: date-time-field
ui.summary: Renders a native datetime-local input.
ui.guidance: datetime-local, not datetime: the value carries no timezone, so the server converts using the user's known zone rather than trusting a browser offset that changes when the user travels.

manifest.name: delivery-status
manifest.title: DeliveryStatus
manifest.description: The DeliveryStatus renderer and its options.

ui.name: delivery-status
ui.summary: Renders a delivery outcome.

manifest.name: description-list
manifest.title: DescriptionList
manifest.description: The DescriptionList renderer and its options.

ui.name: description-list
ui.summary: The read-only detail pattern (account, org).

manifest.name: dialog
manifest.title: Dialog
manifest.description: The Dialog renderer and its options.

ui.name: dialog
ui.summary: Renders a native <dialog>.
ui.guidance: The platform supplies the top layer, the backdrop, the focus trap and Escape-to-close, and the close control is a `form method="dialog"` submit button - so the dialog dismisses with no JavaScript at all. The Alpine `uiDialog` component only calls showModal().
ui.keyboard: Escape closes it: this is a native <dialog>, so the platform supplies dismissal and the focus trap.

manifest.name: disclosure
manifest.title: Disclosure
manifest.description: The Disclosure renderer and its options.

ui.name: disclosure
ui.summary: Renders a native details/summary.
ui.guidance: No JavaScript at all: the platform supplies the toggle, the button semantics, keyboard activation, and the correct announcement of expanded state. It also means the content is present for in-page search and prints expanded when the browser asks it to.

manifest.name: drawer
manifest.title: Drawer
manifest.description: The Drawer renderer and its options.

ui.name: drawer
ui.summary: Renders an edge-anchored modal panel.
ui.guidance: It is a native <dialog>, exactly like Dialog, because the platform supplies the top layer, the backdrop, the focus trap and Escape-to-close. Only the geometry differs, so a drawer that reimplemented any of that would be a second, worse dialog.
ui.keyboard: Escape closes it: this is a native <dialog>, so the platform supplies dismissal and the focus trap.

manifest.name: dropdown-menu
manifest.title: DropdownMenu
manifest.description: The DropdownMenu renderer and its options.

ui.name: dropdown-menu
ui.summary: Renders a button that toggles a panel of links.
ui.guidance: This is a disclosure, not an ARIA menu: it deliberately does not claim role="menu", because that role promises arrow-key navigation between menuitems, and claiming a keyboard contract the widget does not implement is worse for a screen-reader user than presenting an honest expandable button. The panel is a native popover and the trigger opens it declaratively with popovertarget, so the commands disclose, and every link among them works, with no script at all; the platform also supplies light dismiss, Escape and the top layer, so the panel is never clipped by a scrolling table cell. The Alpine component adds focus into the panel on open, focus back to the trigger on close, arrow keys, typeahead, and keeping aria-expanded in step.
ui.keyboard: Focus moves into the panel on open and back to the trigger on close, Escape closes it, ArrowUp/ArrowDown and Home/End move between commands, and a printable character jumps to the next command starting with it.

manifest.name: empty-state
manifest.title: EmptyState
manifest.description: The EmptyState renderer and its options.

ui.name: empty-state
ui.summary: Renders the resting state of a region with no data.
ui.guidance: It carries no role and no live region: an empty list is not news. ErrorState is the announced counterpart for a region that failed.

manifest.name: error-state
manifest.title: ErrorState
manifest.description: The ErrorState renderer and its options.

ui.name: error-state
ui.summary: Renders a failed region with a retry.
ui.guidance: role="alert" because a region that failed after the user acted must be announced - unlike EmptyState, which is a resting state and not news. The retry is a real link with an hx-get, so it works with scripts disabled.

manifest.name: field
manifest.title: Field
manifest.description: The Field renderer and its options.

ui.name: field
ui.summary: Renders label + control + field-level error.
ui.guidance: The control arrives as children so any input type composes, and the hint/error ids come from FieldIDs so a custom control can wire the same aria-describedby.

manifest.name: field-error
manifest.title: FieldError
manifest.description: The FieldError renderer and its options.

ui.name: field-error
ui.summary: The per-field validation message under an input.

manifest.name: fieldset
manifest.title: Fieldset
manifest.description: The Fieldset renderer and its options.

ui.name: fieldset
ui.summary: Groups related fields under a legend.

manifest.name: file-dropzone
manifest.title: FileDropzone
manifest.description: The FileDropzone renderer and its options.

ui.name: file-dropzone
ui.summary: Renders a labelled drop target around a real file input.
ui.guidance: The input is a genuine <input type="file"> inside a <label>, so clicking the zone opens the picker and the keyboard reaches the control with no script at all. Drag-and-drop is added on top by the Alpine behaviour: a drop target that is *only* droppable excludes every keyboard user.

manifest.name: file-input
manifest.title: FileInput
manifest.description: The FileInput renderer and its options.

ui.name: file-input
ui.summary: Renders a native file input.

manifest.name: form
manifest.title: Form
manifest.description: The Form renderer and its options. Renders the hidden CSRF field for every unsafe method, so a form submitted without JavaScript is accepted rather than refused with 403.

ui.name: form
ui.summary: Renders a form wrapper; children are the fields.
ui.guidance: novalidate is always set: server validation is authoritative, and letting the browser block submission first means the server's rules never run. The hidden CSRF field is rendered here, not by callers, for every method the check applies to: the token htmx sends as an inherited request header is unreachable when htmx never loaded, and a form the server then refuses is a worse fallback than no form at all. GET and HEAD forms carry no field - a token in a GET is a token in the URL bar, the history and every access log.

manifest.name: form-actions
manifest.title: FormActions
manifest.description: The FormActions renderer and its options.

ui.name: form-actions
ui.summary: Renders a form's action row.

manifest.name: grid
manifest.title: Grid
manifest.description: The Grid renderer and its options.

ui.name: grid
ui.summary: Renders children in a responsive grid.

manifest.name: hint
manifest.title: Hint
manifest.description: The Hint renderer and its options.

ui.name: hint
ui.summary: Renders help text below a control.

manifest.name: hover-card
manifest.title: HoverCard
manifest.description: The HoverCard renderer and its options.

ui.name: hover-card
ui.summary: Renders a preview that opens on hover *and* focus.
ui.guidance: Focus is not optional: a panel that only opens on hover is unreachable by keyboard and on touch, where there is no hover state at all. The content is a description rather than a label, because the trigger already has a name and replacing it with a paragraph of preview text would make the link unreadable in a screen reader's link list.
ui.keyboard: The trigger is focusable and opens the card on focus as well as hover, and Escape closes it.

manifest.name: inline
manifest.title: Inline
manifest.description: The Inline renderer and its options.

ui.name: inline
ui.summary: Renders children in a horizontal row.

manifest.name: input-addon
manifest.title: InputAddon
manifest.description: The InputAddon renderer and its options.

ui.name: input-addon
ui.summary: Renders a non-editable affix such as a currency symbol or domain suffix.
ui.guidance: It is aria-hidden: the text is a visual hint about the field's format and the field's own label already states what it is, so announcing "dollars" between the label and the value would interrupt the reading.

manifest.name: input-group
manifest.title: InputGroup
manifest.description: The InputGroup renderer and its options.

ui.name: input-group
ui.summary: Joins addons and a control into one visual field.
ui.guidance: The addons are separate elements rather than placeholder text, because placeholder text disappears the moment the user types and was never a label to begin with.

manifest.name: kanban
manifest.title: Kanban board
manifest.description: A board where every card carries a keyboard-operable move menu. Dragging is a shortcut layered on top: it fills and submits the same move form, and the server's response is authoritative.

ui.name: kanban
ui.native_fallback: move buttons in every card's form
ui.summary: Renders the board.
ui.guidance: Dragging is never the only way to move a card, and neither is scripting. Every card renders its destinations as real submit buttons inside the card's own move form, so a move is one click and one POST with nothing but HTML. The keyboard-operable "Move to..." menu offers that same list in a tidier place, and the controller hides the buttons once the menu is operable so one command is not offered twice. The drag is a shortcut on top of both, not a replacement: a board that can only be operated by dragging excludes keyboard users, screen reader users, and anyone on a touch screen where a drag competes with scroll.

ui.name: kanban-card
ui.summary: Renders one card.
ui.guidance: The card is a list item carrying a real form, and that one form is what every path uses: the no-script buttons inside it submit it by navigation, the menu posts the same fields to the same endpoint, and a drag fills in the destination and submits it. The server's response is authoritative, so a rejected move re-renders the board rather than leaving the card where it was dropped.

ui.name: kanban-column
ui.summary: Renders one column and its cards.
ui.guidance: It is a list with a heading, not a generic div: a screen-reader user needs to know how many cards a column holds and where its boundary is, and a list already reports both.

ui.summary: Renders one definition row.

ui.name: item

manifest.name: markdown-editor
manifest.title: Markdown editor
manifest.description: A textarea with Markdown affordances. No WYSIWYG engine and no client-side renderer: the stored value stays Markdown and the preview comes from the server's own goldmark pipeline.

ui.name: editor-preview
ui.summary: Renders the server-rendered preview region.
ui.guidance: It is a polite live region: the preview updates as the author types, and an assertive one would interrupt them mid-sentence. The content arrives from the server's own Markdown pipeline - this component never renders Markdown itself, because a second renderer is a second set of escaping rules.

ui.name: editor-toolbar
ui.summary: Renders the formatting controls.
ui.guidance: Each button carries the Markdown syntax it applies as data, so the controller needs no per-button logic and adding a control is a markup change. The buttons are real buttons with accessible names, not icon-only glyphs: "B" is meaningless read aloud.

ui.name: markdown-editor
ui.summary: Renders a textarea with Markdown affordances.
ui.guidance: The textarea is the form value, always. Every toolbar button and shortcut edits that text in place, so with no JavaScript the author types Markdown into a plain textarea and the form submits unchanged - the toolbar is the part that is optional, not the editing. The toolbar and the media panel are hidden until the controller reveals them: every toolbar control and every media insert writes at the caret, which nothing but the controller can do, and the panel's upload does work without script but would navigate away and abandon whatever the author has typed. A MediaPicker rendered outside an editor stays visible and fully usable; it is this slot that hides, not the picker.
ui.keyboard: Cmd/Ctrl+B, Cmd/Ctrl+I and Cmd/Ctrl+K wrap the selection in bold, italic and link syntax; every other key stays the textarea's own.

ui.name: media-picker
ui.summary: Renders existing media plus an upload control.
ui.guidance: Every item inserts a Markdown image with its alt text already filled in. Alt text is part of the item rather than something the author is prompted for later, because a prompt that can be dismissed produces images with no description. The insert buttons need a controller - they write at the caret - but the upload does not: it is a real file input and a real submit, both owned by the caller's upload form, so choosing a file and sending it works with no script at all.

manifest.title: MemberItem
manifest.description: The MemberItem renderer and its options.

ui.name: member-item
ui.summary: Renders one member row.

manifest.name: mention-chip
manifest.title: MentionChip
manifest.description: The MentionChip renderer and its options.

ui.name: mention-chip
ui.summary: Renders an inline mention.
ui.guidance: The @ is decorative and hidden: a screen reader reading "at Ada Lovelace" inside a sentence is confusing, and the visual marker is what distinguishes a mention from ordinary text for sighted readers.

manifest.name: menubar
manifest.title: Menubar
manifest.description: The Menubar renderer and its options.

ui.name: menubar
ui.summary: Renders application menus as a row of disclosure buttons.
ui.guidance: Each menu is a DropdownMenu, so the whole bar inherits one behaviour: click or Enter to open, Escape to close, focus into the panel and back to the trigger. A real ARIA menubar adds cross-menu arrow navigation and typeahead; building half of that and claiming role="menubar" would promise a keyboard contract the widget does not honour.
ui.keyboard: Click or Enter opens a menu and Escape closes it, with focus moving into the panel and back to the trigger; there is deliberately no cross-menu arrow navigation.

manifest.name: meter
manifest.title: Meter
manifest.description: The Meter renderer and its options.

ui.name: meter
ui.summary: Renders a quota bar with meter semantics.
ui.guidance: role="meter" rather than the native <meter> element: the native element's rendering is controlled by vendor pseudo-elements that differ per browser, so styling it from the token layer is not possible without per-engine hacks. The role gives the same semantics with full control over presentation. It is deliberately not a progressbar. A meter is a measurement inside a range - disk used, seats filled - while a progress bar is a task advancing towards completion. Screen readers announce them differently, and calling a quota a progress bar implies it will finish.

manifest.name: metric
manifest.title: Metric

ui.name: metric
ui.summary: One number on a dashboard.

ui.name: multi-select
ui.summary: Renders a native multiple select.
ui.guidance: Native multiple selection is unloved but it works everywhere, submits without JavaScript, and is understood by every screen reader. The size attribute is set so the list is visible rather than a one-line box the user must discover they can expand.

ui.name: navigation-menu
ui.summary: Renders a labelled group of boosted navigation links.
ui.guidance: These are anchors, not role="menuitem": a menu promises arrow-key navigation and a menu button, while this is a list of links a user tabs through. The honest role is what a screen reader can act on.

manifest.name: notice
manifest.title: Notice
manifest.description: The Notice renderer and its options.

ui.name: notice
ui.summary: An in-page notice inside a form or card.
ui.guidance: Live decides how the message is announced, and the component owns the mapping so a caller cannot silently downgrade an actionable failure to a status. The default is LiveOff: a notice rendered as part of the page on first paint has nothing to announce, and marking it live makes a screen reader read it again on every unrelated update.

ui.name: number-input
ui.summary: Renders a native number input.
ui.guidance: type=number gives the numeric keypad on mobile and the browser's own step controls; reimplementing either in JavaScript would be strictly worse.

manifest.name: onboarding-checklist
manifest.title: OnboardingChecklist
manifest.description: The OnboardingChecklist renderer and its options.

ui.name: onboarding-checklist
ui.summary: Renders setup steps with progress.
ui.guidance: Every step stays visible and actionable once done, rather than disappearing: a list that shrinks as you complete it hides what the product can do, and a user who wants to revisit a step has nowhere to go.

manifest.name: otp-input
manifest.title: OTPInput
manifest.description: The OTPInput renderer and its options.

ui.name: otp-input
ui.summary: Renders a single one-time-code input.
ui.guidance: One input, not one box per digit. A box-per-digit widget breaks paste, breaks password-manager and SMS autofill, and gives a screen reader six unlabelled fields instead of one. autocomplete="one-time-code" is what lets the platform offer the code from a message, and inputmode numeric brings up the keypad.

manifest.name: page-header

ui.guidance: Target is the box the pager morphs; Labels carries the localized strings so ui never imports i18n. A single page renders nothing at all: a pager with both arrows dead is noise that still occupies layout.

manifest.name: panels
manifest.title: Resizable panels
manifest.description: Stacked panels by default; on a wide screen a split with keyboard-operable role=separator handles carrying bounded aria-valuenow.

ui.name: panel
ui.summary: Renders one panel.

ui.name: panel-group
ui.summary: Renders resizable panels.
ui.guidance: The fallback is stacked, full-width panels: with no JavaScript the content is simply laid out one after another, which is also what a narrow screen gets. Resizing is an enhancement on a layout that already works, never the thing that makes the content reachable.
ui.keyboard: The handle is a focusable role="separator": arrow keys move the split by one percent, PageUp/PageDown by ten, and Home/End jump to its bounds.

ui.name: panel-handle
ui.summary: Renders the divider between two panels.
ui.guidance: It is a focusable role="separator" with bounded aria-valuenow, which is what makes the split adjustable by keyboard. A bare styled div would be a pointer-only control, and a separator without the values reports a position of nothing.
ui.keyboard: The handle is a focusable role="separator": arrow keys move the split by one percent, PageUp/PageDown by ten, and Home/End jump to its bounds.

manifest.name: password-input
manifest.title: PasswordInput
manifest.description: The PasswordInput renderer and its options.

ui.name: password-input
ui.summary: Renders a native password field.
ui.guidance: There is no reveal toggle here on purpose: it belongs to a module that owns the Alpine behaviour, and a half-built toggle that leaves the value in the DOM as plain text is worse than none.

manifest.name: plan-card
manifest.title: PlanCard
manifest.description: The PlanCard renderer and its options.

ui.name: plan-card
ui.summary: Renders one plan on the pricing page or in an upgrade CTA.
ui.guidance: Price is pre-formatted by the caller: currency and period formatting is a billing concern, and ui does not import billing.

manifest.name: popover
manifest.title: Popover
manifest.description: The Popover renderer and its options.

ui.name: popover
ui.summary: Renders a trigger with a positioned panel.
ui.guidance: The panel is a native popover opened declaratively with popovertarget, so its content discloses with no script at all - a script-toggled panel would leave arbitrary caller content permanently display:none without one. The platform supplies light dismiss, Escape and the top layer; the Alpine component adds only the focus handling and keeps aria-expanded in step, because a declarative popovertarget button does not write that attribute and an expandable button that never reports its state is a bug.
ui.keyboard: Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger. A popover holds arbitrary content, so it makes no promise about arrow or typeahead navigation inside it: those keys belong to whatever the panel contains, and a menu that needs them is DropdownMenu.

manifest.name: progress-bar
manifest.title: ProgressBar
manifest.description: The ProgressBar renderer and its options.

ui.name: progress-bar
ui.summary: Renders task progress with progressbar semantics.
ui.guidance: progressbar, not meter: a progress bar describes a task advancing towards completion, while a meter describes a measurement within a range. Screen readers announce them differently, and using meter for a running task tells the user a quota is filling up.

manifest.name: progress-circle
manifest.title: ProgressCircle
manifest.description: The ProgressCircle renderer and its options.

ui.name: progress-circle
ui.summary: Renders progress as a ring.
ui.guidance: The ring is drawn with an SVG stroke offset and is aria-hidden; the semantics live on the wrapper, so assistive technology gets a progressbar with a value rather than a description of two circles.

manifest.name: questionnaire
manifest.title: Questionnaire
manifest.description: Native fields and a server-owned step. Each step posts its answer and the server decides what comes next, so a reload resumes rather than restarts.

ui.name: question
ui.summary: Renders one question's native control.
ui.guidance: Radio and checkbox sets are a fieldset with a legend, because the question is the group's label: without it a screen reader reads the options with no idea what is being asked.

ui.name: questionnaire
ui.summary: Renders one step of a questionnaire.
ui.guidance: State lives on the server. A wizard that keeps answers in the browser loses them on reload, cannot be resumed on another device, and cannot be validated - so each step posts its answer and the server decides what comes next.

ui.name: wizard-actions
ui.summary: Renders Back, Skip and Next/Submit.
ui.guidance: The naming stays consistent across every step: the forward control is "Next" until the final step, where it is the submit verb. Changing the wording mid-flow makes the user re-read the button on every step to check what it now does.

ui.summary: Renders a bounded, keyboard-scrollable region.
ui.guidance: tabindex="0" plus role="region" is the pairing that matters. A scrollable div with neither is reachable only by pointer, so its content is unreadable to a keyboard user once it overflows.
ui.keyboard: The region is focusable, so arrow keys and Page Up/Down scroll its content for a keyboard user.

manifest.name: search-input
manifest.title: SearchInput
manifest.description: The SearchInput renderer and its options. The field lives inside its own GET form, so the query can be sent with no scripting at all.

ui.name: search-input
ui.summary: The debounced table search, inside its own GET form.
ui.guidance: It morphs Target and pushes the URL, so a search is shareable and the Back button works. The form is not decoration: a bare input has no submit path whatsoever, so with no scripting the query the user typed cannot leave the page. The form gives the browser the same job htmx does - send Name to GetURL - and any parameters GetURL already carries travel as hidden fields, because a native GET submit replaces the query string rather than adding to it. The submit control is visually hidden until focused: a permanently visible button beside a field that filters as you type says the live filtering does not work, and a button that only exists in JavaScript is one a keyboard or no-script user cannot reach.

manifest.name: secret-reveal

ui.name: section

manifest.name: settings-section
manifest.title: SettingsSection
manifest.description: The SettingsSection renderer and its options.

ui.name: settings-section
ui.summary: Renders a titled settings block.

manifest.name: skeleton
manifest.title: Skeleton
manifest.description: The Skeleton renderer and its options.

ui.name: skeleton
ui.summary: Renders a loading placeholder.
ui.guidance: Always aria-hidden, with no exception: a screen reader announcing "loading, loading, loading" for a stack of grey boxes is worse than silence, and the region's own live announcement is what should report arrival. It is only for an *initially empty* region - drawing skeletons over content that is already on screen replaces real information with fake information.

manifest.name: skip-link
manifest.title: SkipLink
manifest.description: The SkipLink renderer and its options.

ui.name: skip-link
ui.summary: Renders the first focusable control on the page.

It must be the first control in the document, otherwise a keyboard user tabs through the whole navigation before reaching the way to bypass it.

manifest.name: slug-input

ui.name: slug-input
ui.summary: Renders a text input that mirrors another field until edited.
ui.guidance: It is a plain text input first: with no JavaScript the user types the slug themselves and the form works. The Alpine behaviour only stops mirroring once the user edits the slug directly, because silently overwriting what someone typed is worse than not helping at all.

ui.summary: Renders a state dot with its label.

manifest.name: steps
manifest.title: Steps

ui.name: steps
ui.summary: Renders an ordered progress trail.
ui.guidance: The position is stated in text ("Step 2 of 4") rather than left to the styling: colour and a filled circle are invisible to a screen reader and ambiguous to anyone who cannot distinguish the two shades.

manifest.name: sticky-bar
manifest.title: StickyBar
manifest.description: The StickyBar renderer and its options.

ui.name: sticky-bar
ui.summary: Renders a pinned action bar.
ui.guidance: It is sticky rather than fixed, so it stays inside its scroll container and cannot cover content the container has scrolled past. A fixed bar overlays the viewport, which on a short screen can hide the very field its Save button submits.

manifest.name: switch
manifest.title: Switch
manifest.description: The Switch renderer and its options.

ui.name: switch
ui.summary: A labelled toggle.

manifest.name: tab-panels
manifest.title: TabPanels
manifest.description: The TabPanels renderer and its options.

ui.name: tab-panels
ui.summary: Renders the ARIA tab widget.
ui.guidance: This is the one navigation component that genuinely needs script, and it claims role="tablist" only because it implements the whole contract: a single tab stop for the set (roving tabindex), Left/Right to move between tabs, Home/End to jump to the ends, and aria-selected plus aria-controls wiring the tab to its panel. NavTabs is the alternative for navigation between URLs - tabs that are really links should stay links. The server renders the fallback rather than the enhanced state: every panel open, in order, with the tab bar hidden. Collapsing to one panel before the controller exists would lose every panel but the first, and offering tabs only a controller can operate would be a row of dead buttons; uiTabs reveals the bar and collapses to the selected panel on init.
ui.keyboard: A roving tabindex gives the set one tab stop; Left/Right move and activate the adjacent tab, and Home/End jump to the first or last.

manifest.name: table-toolbar

The pre-paint script in the document head sets the initial class, so the page never flashes the wrong theme; this control flips it and persists the result. manifest.title: Timeline

ui.name: timeline
ui.summary: Renders events in order.

manifest.title: Toast
manifest.description: The Toast renderer and its options.

ui.name: toast
ui.summary: Renders a transient message.

manifest.name: toast-region
manifest.title: Toast region
manifest.description: The ToastRegion renderer and its options.

ui.name: toast-region
ui.summary: Renders the shell's live toast stack.
ui.guidance: One per document, rendered in the shell and outside #content: navigation swaps only #content, so a region inside it would be destroyed mid-swap and lose both its queued toasts and its document listener. The live-region semantics sit on the container rather than on each toast, because a live region has to exist before its message arrives or nothing is announced. Its Alpine controller (toastRoot) is registered by the shell in static/app.js: the shell owns the HX-Trigger listener and the flash handoff across a redirect.

manifest.title: Toolbar
manifest.description: The Toolbar renderer and its options.

ui.name: toolbar
ui.summary: Renders a group of related controls.
ui.guidance: role="group", not role="toolbar": a toolbar promises arrow-key navigation between its controls with a single tab stop. These controls are each tabbable, so claiming toolbar would advertise a keyboard contract that is not implemented.

manifest.name: tooltip
manifest.title: Tooltip
manifest.description: The Tooltip renderer and its options.

ui.name: tooltip
ui.summary: Renders an inline tooltip on hover/focus.
ui.guidance: The trigger is the caller's own element (children), so this renderer cannot put aria-describedby on it; the text is exposed with role="tooltip" and the association belongs to the trigger-owning API in the component catalog.

manifest.name: tree
manifest.title: Tree

ui.name: tree
ui.summary: Renders a disclosure tree.
ui.guidance: It is built from nested `details` elements, so with no JavaScript every branch still opens and every leaf is still reachable. The controller adds the APG keyboard model on top - roving focus, arrows, Home/End and typeahead - by upgrading this markup rather than replacing it. A div-based tree would have to implement disclosure, keyboard and semantics all at once, and would offer nothing when any of the three failed.
ui.keyboard: A roving tabindex gives the tree one tab stop; ArrowUp/ArrowDown move between visible nodes, ArrowRight opens a branch or steps into it, ArrowLeft closes it or steps out, Home/End jump to the ends, and printable characters start typeahead.

ui.name: tree-grid
ui.summary: Renders a hierarchy with columns.
ui.guidance: This is a table, because the data is rows and columns and a table already reports both. Depth is carried by aria-level on each row rather than by indentation alone: indentation is a visual convention that conveys nothing to a screen reader, and "level 3" is the fact the user needs.

ui.name: tree-node
ui.summary: Renders one node and its children.

operations.description:
Newest first. Two pagination modes share one response shape:

- **`cursor` (preferred)** — keyset paging. Follow `next_cursor` from
  the previous response. Stable under concurrent writes: a cursor
  names a row, so projects created while you page do not shift rows
  across page boundaries, and depth costs nothing server-side.
- **`offset` (legacy)** — the original contract, still honoured. It
  repeats or drops rows when the set changes mid-walk.

`next_cursor` is `null` on the last page. Cursors are opaque: echo
them back verbatim, never parse or construct them.

parameters.description: Page size. Values outside 1–100 fall back to the default.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description:
Opaque position from a previous response's `next_cursor`.
Takes precedence over `offset`. A malformed value is rejected
with 400 rather than silently restarting at the first page.

parameters.description:
Legacy. Rows to skip; negative values are treated as 0. Ignored
when `cursor` is supplied.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

info.description:
The second transport. Every rule the HTML app enforces (plan limits,
validation, org scoping) applies identically here — the handlers share
the same query layer and plan logic, they only differ in how they answer.

Authentication is a Bearer token minted at `/app/settings/api`
(`ggg_…`, SHA-256 hashed at rest, shown once). Tokens carry a scope:
`read` satisfies read operations, `write` satisfies both.

The token determines the organization — there is no org parameter, and a
token can never read another org's rows.
